title: Chocolate shards and plaques for cake decoration
subtitle: Thin poured chocolate panels and shards for finishing layer cakes
excerpt: Chocolate shards and plaques are made by spreading melted chocolate thinly onto baking paper, leaving it to set, then breaking or cutting it into shapes. They add height and texture to layer cakes and need no special equipment beyond a palette knife and a flat surface. Tempered chocolate gives a cleaner snap; untempered chocolate still works for most home cake decoration.
sourceNotes: Chocolate shards and set-chocolate panels are a widely taught home cake-decorating technique. The basic method requires no specialised equipment.

recipe.yieldDescription: Shards and plaques for one layer cake
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the shards up to 1 week ahead. Store between layers of baking paper in a cool, dry place. Do not refrigerate; condensation will bloom the surface.

glossaryTerms.definition: A white or grey streaky film on the surface of chocolate caused by fat or sugar migrating to the surface. Fat bloom results from unstable cocoa butter (unchilled chocolate); sugar bloom from condensation. Both are harmless but affect appearance.

content.text: Chocolate shards are made by spreading melted chocolate thinly on baking paper, allowing it to set, then breaking it into irregular pieces. Plaques are cut into neat rectangles or triangles before the chocolate fully sets. Both are quick to make and transform a simple buttercream cake into something that looks carefully finished.
Melt 150 g dark or milk chocolate in a bowl over barely simmering water. Stir until smooth. Remove from the heat.
Pour onto a sheet of baking paper. Spread with an icing spatula to 2 to 3 mm thickness. Spread in one direction for neat, roughly rectangular shards; spread in wavy strokes for organic shapes.
Leave at room temperature (around 18°C) for 30 minutes or until the chocolate is firm to the touch but not brittle. Do not refrigerate, this causes
Lift the sheet and snap the chocolate into irregular pieces. Press the shards at angles into the frosted cake.

For plaques, spread the chocolate as above. When it begins to set (slightly tacky but no longer glossy and liquid), use a sharp knife to cut into rectangles or other shapes. Leave to set fully, then peel off the paper. Plaques can be marked with initials or a pattern at this semi-set stage using a toothpick.

Sprinkle gold leaf, edible lustre dust, or crushed freeze-dried fruit over the spread chocolate before it sets. For a marbled effect, drizzle a contrasting chocolate (dark over white, or white over dark) and swirl with a skewer before the base sets.
